# `kernel/navi/NaviModelBroker.js`

> **Source:** `webgpu-os/kernel/navi/NaviModelBroker.js`

NaviModelBroker.js — deterministic, per-Navi model selection and failover. The broker owns no provider conversation and executes no tools. It chooses one declared cognition route, invokes the injected AI Hub exactly once at a time, and only advances to a bounded fallback after a retryable model-call failure. Prompt/model output is deliberately excluded from routing evidence.

## Functions

### `async verifyNaviModelRouteDecision(rawDecision, rawConfiguration)`

Verify that a projected route decision is the exact content-addressed decision produced for the supplied normalized broker configuration. This is an integrity/binding check only; it never authorizes model use.

### `normalizeModelFailure(source, signal = null)`

### `normalizeNaviModelRequirements(raw = {}, purpose = 'chat')`

Return the broker's exact model-neutral requirement evidence. Resource selection receipts must hash the same defaults and canonical ordering that `decide()` used; callers must not reconstruct those defaults independently.

### `normalizeNaviModelRouteConfiguration(raw, { now = null } = {})`

Normalize the complete route configuration through the broker's authoritative schema. Read-only consumers use this boundary to validate the exact candidate shape instead of maintaining a second, drifting schema. Freshness remains opt-in because execution performs its own live evidence check immediately before dispatch.

## Notes & Examples

### Command Bus Pattern

The OS uses a capability-gated command bus for inter-app and system communication. Apps register command handlers; the kernel routes commands based on capabilities. Commands can be local (same app), cross-app (with permission), or system-level (elevated).

**Example: Command registration and invocation**
```js
import { CommandBus } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/CommandBus.js';
import { Capability } from 'webgpu-os/kernel/Capability.js';

const bus = new CommandBus();

// Register a handler (requires 'ui' capability)
bus.register('myapp:openFile', async (path) => {
  const content = await storage.read(path);
  return { content, size: content.length };
}, { capability: 'storage' });

// Invoke locally
const result = await bus.invoke('myapp:openFile', '/docs/readme.md');

// Cross-app invocation (requires 'interop' capability)
const otherApp = bus.proxy('otherapp');
const data = await otherApp.invoke('otherapp:compute', input);

// Broadcast to all listening apps
bus.broadcast('system:themeChanged', { theme: 'dark' });
```

**See also:** [WebGPU OS Architecture](/webgpu-os/architecture.md) · [Security Model](/concepts/security-model.md)
